question.latex: For a given circuit the time dependent input voltage $v_{in}$t$$ is a sine wave alternating between $20\text{V}$ and $-20\text{V}$. The corresponding output $v_o$t$$ is clipped flat at $+5\text{V}$ and $-5\text{V}$. Identify the components that are used in the circuit in the parallel branch between points X and Y to produce this clipped output.
question.unicode: For a given circuit the time dependent input voltage v_{in}t is a sine wave alternating between 20text{V} and -20text{V}. The corresponding output v_ot is clipped flat at +5text{V} and -5text{V}. Identify the components that are used in the circuit in the parallel branch between points X and Y to produce this clipped output.
question.plainText: For a given circuit the time dependent input voltage v_{in}t is a sine wave alternating between 20text{V} and -20text{V}. The corresponding output v_ot is clipped flat at +5text{V} and -5text{V}. Identify the components that are used in the circuit in the parallel branch between points X and Y to produce this clipped output.

options.latex: A resistor and a Zener diode
options.unicode: A resistor and a Zener diode
options.plainText: A resistor and a Zener diode

explanation.latex:
The output voltage $v_o(t)$ is a clipped version of the input, restricted symmetrically to $+5\text{V}$ and $-5\text{V}$. 
To achieve bidirectional symmetric voltage clipping, two Zener diodes must be connected back-to-back (in series, but pointing in opposite directions) across the output terminals.
During the positive half-cycle, one Zener diode is forward biased and acts like a normal diode, while the other is reverse biased and experiences Zener breakdown at its $V_Z = 5\text{V}$, holding the voltage constant.
During the negative half-cycle, their roles reverse, successfully clipping the output at $-5\text{V}$. Thus, two back-to-back Zener diodes are required.
